headline: Your Walk-In Tells Me More About Your Kitchen Than Your Menu
deck: Storage, labels, rotation and organization expose the systems behind the food before I taste a single plate.
author: Josh Freeman
heroImageAlt: Commercial refrigeration inside a working kitchen
body: A menu can be polished in an afternoon. A walk-in cannot hide the way a kitchen actually operates.

Look at labels, dates, raw-over-ready-to-eat storage, open containers, duplicated prep, forgotten produce and how easy it is for a cook to find what they need. Those details tell you whether the operation has a system or is surviving on memory.
Food cost, safety and speed all show up in the same room. That is why organization is not cosmetic.
joshTake: If I am trying to understand a kitchen fast, I want five minutes in the walk-in before I want five minutes with the menu.
seoTitle: What Your Walk-In Says About Your Kitchen
seoDescription: Why walk-in organization reveals food cost, food safety and kitchen-system problems faster than a menu does.
